timing_scope: User-supplied 10 minute closeout slice for the exp1269/exp1270 paper and arXiv path, not the full research milestone.
summary: Milestone 2026.04.99 closeout was efficient in wall-clock terms: 10 minutes total for 2 completed items, averaging 5 minutes each. The only material slow path was exp1270 arXiv Bundle v10, which was correctly gated on exp1269 critical paper fixes. GPU utilization was inefficient for the broader milestone because both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout, but no zombie process was wasting material VRAM. Pre-flight checks and docs reconciliation were not measured bottlenecks in this slice; the remaining leverage is better parallel scheduling, cached TeX/pre-flight state, structured timing, and idempotent ops-doc updates.

milestone_research_context.note: Research outcome context only; operational timing analysis uses the supplied 10 minute closeout slice.

slowest_experiments.title: arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_slow: This was the only nonzero closeout item. It was on the publication critical path, waited for exp1269 critical fixes, then compiled docs/arxiv-paper/main.tex with tectonic and wrote results/carnot-arxiv-v10-20260504.tar.gz. The artifact shows TeX font/package downloads during compilation, so cached TeX state would likely trim future runs.
slowest_experiments.parallelizable: Not before exp1269 completed; after the gate passed, packaging and upload-readiness checks could be split from ops-doc reconciliation.

slowest_experiments.title: In-process docs for arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_slow: No measured runtime in the supplied timing block. It was not a bottleneck in this closeout slice.
slowest_experiments.parallelizable: Yes. Changelog, status, roadmap, and artifact summaries can be reconciled asynchronously after terminal experiment artifacts are written.

gpu_state.assessment: Inefficient for a dual-GPU research milestone: both GPUs were idle with only driver-residual 4 MB allocations. There were no gpu_monitor.py-class zombies, but the scheduler left available GPU capacity unused.

question_answers.which_experiments_took_longest_and_why: exp1270 took the full measured 10 minutes because it sat on the exp1269 paper-fix gate and then performed the arXiv compile/package path. The docs item measured 0 minutes and was not slow.
question_answers.was_gpu_utilization_efficient: No. Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout, 4 MB used and 0 percent utilization on each. For this paper-bundle slice GPU demand was low, but the broader milestone should schedule independent SOTA/GPU work through DualGPURunner instead of leaving both cards idle.
question_answers.were_there_zombie_processes_wasting_reso: No. scripts/gpu_monitor.py --json reported an empty process list and no warnings. The 4 MB per GPU allocation appears to be residual driver state, not a zombie workload.
question_answers.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: Yes. exp1270 itself could not start before exp1269, but docs reconciliation, artifact validation, and upload-readiness checks could run after the gate in parallel. Independent GPU/SOTA experiments from the broader .99 milestone should be split across GPU 0 and GPU 1.
question_answers.was_the_pre_flight_test_suite_a_bottlene: No evidence in this slice. Existing .99 ops notes record seconds-scale checks, including 81 tests in 8.24s and 7.89s, which is negligible relative to even a 10 minute closeout.
question_answers.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: Operationally lightweight in the timing block, but not fully efficient as a process: repeated .99 retro/changelog/roadmap entries show the need for idempotent upserts and duplicate detection. The work should be batched after terminal artifacts, not repeated by every recovery run.
question_answers.what_tooling_infrastructure_changes_woul: Add conductor-native structured timing for gate, compile, test, docs, and artifact phases; cache TeX and pre-flight state; emit terminal gate-block artifacts immediately; schedule independent GPU lanes with DualGPURunner; and make ops-doc reconciliation idempotent.

bottlenecks_identified: Publication critical path was serialized: exp1270 correctly waited for exp1269, so the arXiv bundle could not be parallelized before the gate passed.
Dual RTX 3090 capacity was idle at closeout despite available GPU experiments in the wider milestone class.
TeX compilation incurred cache/download overhead during exp1270, visible in the tectonic stdout tail.
Conductor timing is too coarse: the supplied slice reports total item minutes but not separate gate, compile, package, validation, and docs durations.
Ops-doc reconciliation is not idempotent enough; existing .99 changelog and roadmap entries show duplicate closeout rows from repeated recovery passes.
Gate-blocked experiments still risk missing or null terminal artifacts, as seen in the broader .99 retro context for exp1277.
improvements_suggested: Use DualGPURunner by default for independent SOTA/GPU experiments: Qwen on GPU 0, Gemma on GPU 1, with active queueing while CPU/docs tasks run.
Pre-warm and persist TeX state for arXiv bundle runs so font/package downloads do not occur inside the timed closeout path.
Record structured per-phase timing in the conductor: gate_wait_s, preflight_s, compile_s, package_s, docs_s, artifact_write_s, and upload_wait_s.
Emit a terminal JSON artifact for every blocked or gated experiment, including explicit blocked_reason and upstream field values, instead of leaving absent/null artifacts.
Make changelog and roadmap reconciliation idempotent by matching on milestone plus retro_type/theme before appending new rows.
Batch docs reconciliation after all terminal artifacts exist, and run JSON validation before changelog/roadmap edits.
Move upload-readiness checks into a small reusable script that verifies PDF, tarball, size, required files, and arXiv blocker state in one fast pass.
estimated_time_savings_basis: The 10 minute slice is already short, so savings are mostly from preventing repeated recovery/docs passes and keeping future GPU work parallel. Expected reduction for similar closeout slices is about 3 minutes; the broader next milestone can save more when independent GPU work is present.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions.action: Add structured conductor phase timing plus terminal blocked artifacts
top_3_highest_leverage_actions.reason: Makes the true slow phase visible and prevents retries or retros from reverse-engineering gate state.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions.action: Pre-warm TeX/pre-flight caches before publication closeout
top_3_highest_leverage_actions.reason: Removes avoidable package/font downloads and repeated seconds-scale checks from the critical path.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions.action: Use DualGPURunner and async docs reconciliation for independent work
top_3_highest_leverage_actions.reason: Keeps both RTX 3090s busy while CPU/doc tasks proceed and prevents docs updates from serializing research throughput.

verification.notes: JSON validation is recorded after final file write.

meta_reflection: The process improvements for .99 are less about shortening exp1270 itself and more about avoiding repeated recovery passes. Skeleton-first artifacts worked as intended, but repeated .99 closeout entries reveal that the next operational gain is idempotent finalization: one terminal artifact, one changelog bullet, one roadmap row, and machine-readable timing for every phase.
